answer: Give every agent one TPM-bound identity card: its key never leaves the chip, so one chip means one identity. Four steps: the agent signs a challenge with the chip to prove ownership; a copper seal binds that card to one wallet; peers check the chip certificate before accepting work; and a delta scan compares new registrations against known chips to flag duplicates. Forging 10,000 fakes needs 10,000 chips at $40 each and 30 days of checks, a $400,000 wall before a fake vote lands. Like a bridge open only to plated vehicles, the network admits only hardware it can inspect.
